tier_reason: First-party benchmark only: the Criterion bench code is public (compare/tests/compare.rs, with the bench profile in compare/Cargo.toml) and the linked Google Sheet gives per-hasher timings, but no CPU model and no rustc version are stated. The one independent suite, rurban/SMHasher, does not back the win: it shows aHash losing about 2x on bulk throughput to xxh3 and wyhash and winning only slightly on small keys, so this cannot be B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Page text (verbatim): "AHash is faster than either one [t1ha and XXHash], both with and without AES"; "AHash outperforms wyHash across all input sizes"; "At over 50GB/s aHash is the fastest algorithm to pass the full test suite by more than a factor of 2"; about 10x faster than SipHash. The Google Sheet linked from the page gives time to hash a u64 and a 1 KB string (units not labelled, probably ns): AHash 0.87 / 19.98, XXHash (xxh3) 11.88 / 114.14, WyHash 1.53 / 53.13, SipHash-1-3 9.70 / 219.13, FxHash 0.71 / 121.97. That makes aHash about 13.7x / 5.7x faster than xxh3, 1.76x / 2.66x faster than wyhash, and 11x / 11x faster than SipHash-1-3 (derived from page data).
corrections.baseline: xxHash (XXH3 via xxhash-rust) and wyhash; also SipHash-1-3, the Rust std HashMap default
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc (version unstated); bench profile in compare/Cargo.toml: opt-level=3, lto='fat', codegen-units=1, debug-assertions=false; Criterion 0.3.3; target-cpu/RUSTFLAGS unstated
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1347 GitHub stars; about 790M crates.io downloads (about 151M recent) and 2051 reverse dependencies. It was hashbrown's default hasher until hashbrown v0.15.0 (2024-10), which switched to foldhash. It was never the Rust std HashMap default, which is SipHash-1-3.
corrections.workload: Criterion microbenchmarks that hash a u64 and strings of 1-1023 bytes through Rust's Hasher/BuildHasher trait (compare/tests/compare.rs), compared with SipHash, FxHash, FnvHash, FarmHash, HighwayHash, MetroHash, t1ha, xxh3 and wyhash. The "50GB/s" figure comes from the SMHasher bulk test (smhasher/ahashOutput.txt: 60349 MiB/s average at a nominal "3 ghz")
corrections.caveats: No CPU model or rustc version is stated, and the sheet does not label its time units. Comparisons go through Rust Hasher-trait wrappers, which may penalise streaming hashes such as xxh3 on 1 KB inputs. The independent rurban/SMHasher table (AMD Ryzen 5 3350G) contradicts the bulk-speed claims: ahash64 9862.62 MiB/s against xxh3 20853.74 and wyhash 22640.53. It shows aHash only slightly ahead on small keys (27.32 cycles/hash against 29.46 for xxh3 and 28.91 for wyhash). The "fastest SMHasher-passing algorithm by >2x" claim is stale. Output is not stable across platforms or versions (HashMap use only). FxHash is faster on u64 keys, as the page admits.

notes: The quotes in the record match the page word for word. The record understated the evidence: the linked sheet does have tabular numbers. Fixed the license (the repo is dual MIT/Apache-2.0, not just Apache-2.0) and the usage claim, since aHash was hashbrown's default hasher until v0.15 and was never the std default. Independent SMHasher data contradicts the bulk-throughput superiority claim, so tier stays C with a strong caveat.
